title: dangote oil refinery buys 16 million barrels nigerian crude october sources say 2026 09 10
text:
LONDON, Sept 10 (Reuters) - Nigeria’s Dangote refinery has bought at least 16 million barrels of Nigerian crude for October arrival, according to four industry sources, in line with recent months and much higher ​than last year's average as Africa's largest refinery ramps up processing.
Dangote's ​16 million barrels, made up of monthly allocations from Nigerian ⁠National Petroleum Company and volumes bought in a tender, equal around 520,000 ​barrels per day. That accounts for most of the 700,000-bpd refinery’s monthly intake.
The ​plant is preparing for an initial public offering, in which feedstock supply is in focus for investors. Its purchases will curb volumes of Nigerian crude available for export at a time ​of high demand due to the Iran war drastically cutting competing supply ​from the Middle East.
The final total may rise if Dangote procures more crude. Dangote did ‌not ⁠respond to a request for comment.
The Lagos-based refiner received 565,000 bpd of Nigerian crude in August, according to Kpler data, nearly double last year's average of 280,000 bpd.
In total, NNPC will supply Dangote with eight of its October ​Nigerian cargoes, and ​one U.S. WTI ⁠Midland cargo, a source familiar with the matter said.
That would equal the monthly record for NNPC supply to the ​refinery, after it provided a similar volume in April, May ​and ⁠August, Kpler data show.
The refinery bought a second WTI cargo for October from a different supplier in a spot tender, two traders said, as well as the ⁠extra ​Nigerian cargoes to make up the total of ​16 million barrels.
Dangote has bought many different grades of crude from outside Nigeria, including from Libya ​and Guyana.
